theorem harmonic_closedBall_mean_value {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n)
    (u : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ)
    (a : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) (r : ℝ) (hr : 0 < r)
    (hu : ∃ v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ,
      InnerProductSpace.HarmonicOnNhd v (Metric.closedBall a r) ∧
      Set.EqOn v u (Metric.closedBall a r)) :
    let τ : MeasureTheory.Measure (Metric.sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) 1) :=
      (MeasureTheory.volume : MeasureTheory.Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))).toSphere
    (∫ ζ : Metric.sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) 1,
      u (a + r • (ζ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))) ∂((τ Set.univ)⁻¹ • τ)) = u a

binder_audit.n: TYPING natural dimension of standard real Euclidean carrier
binder_audit.hn: STANDING HFT n>1, exactly 2<=n for natural n
binder_audit.u: TYPING total real-valued representative of source values on the closed ball; all values outside the closed ball are unconstrained and irrelevant.
binder_audit.hu: SOURCE existence of a harmonic extension on a neighborhood of the closed ball, encoded by a total neighborhood representative v and EqOn v u on that closed ball. This is the source closed-set definition, not an extra proof ingredient or regularity condition on arbitrary off-ball values of u.

definition_audit.harmonicity: The source extension witness v is genuinely Mathlib HarmonicOnNhd near the closed ball; EqOn constrains only source-domain values. HarmonicAt is open, so the witness is harmonic on an open neighborhood. No regularity or ambient measurability is imposed on u outside the closed ball. Real-valued specialization remains explicit.
definition_audit.surface_measure: Literal Euclidean volume.toSphere on the unit-sphere subtype, normalized by its total mass. Its finite nonzero mass and identification with the source normalized surface law must be justified from n>=2 and existing canonical measure facts, not assumed.
definition_audit.integral: Actual Bochner integral of u(a+r*zeta) over the normalized sphere. The argument lies in the closed ball; its values agree with the harmonic witness. Derive restricted integrability and transfer the conclusion; no totalized integral shortcut.
definition_audit.dimension_routes: Both the source n>2 fundamental-solution and n=2 logarithm routes remain in the source graph. No arbitrary-dimensional conclusion may be inferred from the complex-plane theorem.
